assessments.zone: Yahisuli secteur villages south of the Congo river toward Opala (Yahisuli health zone)
assessments.evidence: Remote forest secteur with no reported armed-group activity; default state presence. Background knowledge only.

assessments.zone: Yakusu secteur villages on the Congo river and Kisangani-Isangi road (Yakusu and Yaleko health zones: Yanonge, Yaongonda/Yubo, Yandjoku, Yamenga, Ilota)
assessments.evidence: Peri-Kisangani river and road villages with no reported armed-group activity; default state presence. Background knowledge only.

assessments.zone: Rural villages of Isangi and Yabaondo secteurs (Isangi and Yabaondo health zones, Isangi-Yabaondo/Bolinga roads, Lomami and Aruwimi riverside villages)
assessments.evidence: No reported armed-group presence; state presence assumed via PNC posts and chieftaincy authorities. Background knowledge only.

assessments.zone: Isangi town (territorial seat on the Congo river at the Lomami/Aruwimi confluence; Kunda / Yalosase health area and adjacent quarters)
assessments.evidence: Territorial administration seat with PNC commissariat and courts; no reports of armed-group activity known. Assessment from background knowledge; web research unavailable.

assessments.zone: Yangambi town and INERA research station area (Inera, Lomboto, Lusambila, Ekutsu health areas)
assessments.evidence: Cité hosting INERA and the Yangambi biosphere reserve, policed by PNC with ICCN/eco-guards for the reserve; no armed-group control known. Background knowledge only.

units.CD5105-isangi: Isangi territory (Tshopo), west of Kisangani along the Congo river at the Lomami and Aruwimi confluences, lies far from the eastern Kivu/Ituri conflict zones and no armed group is known to hold or administer any part of it as of the reference date. The state administers Isangi town (territorial seat) and Yangambi (INERA research centre and biosphere reserve), where the Congolese National Police (PNC) is the main day-to-day security force with a small FARDC presence. Rural villages of the Isangi, Yabaondo, Yakusu and Yahisuli secteurs are assessed under default state presence; local land, chieftaincy and boundary disputes and occasional banditry or poaching on the river are not known to have produced lasting non-state control. Web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites egress-blocked), so confidence is medium for the towns and low elsewhere.
